title: Claude model roster — source of record
description: Canonical source of record for the selectable Claude model set: one row per pinned full model ID, keyed by that ID, carrying the vendor facts (context window, output cap, knowledge cutoff, minimum cacheable prefix, batch discount, price) together with the fields that let every consumer be a runtime read or a generated artifact instead of a hand-maintained copy (family, generation, effort availability, effort exemption, lifecycle, selectability, cross-family ordering). INPUTS: this schema plus the authored roster document; a consumer additionally supplies a lookup key — a pinned full model ID that MAY carry a trailing `-YYYYMMDD` snapshot suffix and/or a `[1m]` window selector, both of which MUST be stripped before lookup, since neither ever appears in a row key. OUTPUTS, each a projection of the rows and never a hand-kept list: the plan-schema model enum = ids with `selectable == "new-work"` plus every `effort_exempt_sentinels` entry; the model-authoring gate's allowlist = ids with `selectable != "retired"` and no sentinels (a sentinel is not a model); an effort-availability table = ids whose `effort_available` contains that level; the effort-check exemption list = ids with `effort_exempt == true` plus every `effort_exempt_sentinels` entry; the rate table = rows with a non-null price, a consumer preferring `price.contract` over `price.list` whenever the former is present; and a capability comparison between two ids. INVARIANTS: (1) a lookup key with no row resolves to the distinct `roster-stale` outcome naming the refresh action — never to "below floor", "unsupported", or a deny-all; a missing or unreadable roster document is itself roster-stale, never an implicit deny. (2) Ordering WITHIN a family is DERIVED by comparing `generation` element-wise — the first differing element decides, and a prefix ranks below its extension, so [5] outranks [4,8] and [5,1] outranks [5] — and is never stored. (3) Ordering ACROSS families comes only from `cross_family_rank` (higher is more capable), is defined only when BOTH rows declare one, and an undeclared pair is a roster-stale-class error: never a default, a guess, or a fallback to any other field. (4) Among rows that declare one, `cross_family_rank` is unique, and within a family it increases with `generation`. (5) A same-family comparison ignores `cross_family_rank` entirely. (6) `lifecycle` and `selectable` are INDEPENDENT axes — lifecycle is the vendor's active/deprecated state, selectable is this workspace's new-work/legacy-pin-only/retired policy — so no consumer derives one from the other; the enum projection and the allowlist projection are required to be able to disagree, and today do. (7) `effort_exempt_sentinels` contains `inherit`: it is a dispatch sentinel, not a model, and never gets a row; a generated exemption list narrower than the one this document projects is a failure. (8) A row's `family` and `generation` agree with the segments of its key. (9) A null vendor-fact field means "no vendor value sourced in this refresh" — never zero, unlimited, or free; a consumer that needs the value resolves roster-stale. (10) `_schema_version` is this schema's MAJOR: a consumer refuses a document whose `_schema_version` exceeds the version it was built against, and within a MAJOR only additive optional fields appear. (11) The document is canonical JSON — keys sorted, two-space indent, LF endings, one trailing newline — so re-emitting a parsed roster is byte-identical to the file on disk.

_schema_version.description: MAJOR version of this schema. A consumer built against version N refuses a document declaring more than N (forward-refusal) rather than reading unknown semantics; within a MAJOR, only additive optional fields are introduced, so a consumer built against N reads any N document.

_as_of.description: Date the vendor facts in this document were last verified against their sources.

_source.description: Provenance for the vendor facts: which vendor pages supplied which fields, when they were fetched, and any field-level caveat a refresh must re-check.

_unit.description: Unit for every price figure in the document. Prices are unitless numbers without it.

_cross_family_order.description: Provenance for the declared cross-family ordering, carried here so a consumer never re-derives it and a re-verification knows which pairs have a citation. Pairs involving a row with a null `cross_family_rank` are undeclared and resolve roster-stale.

as_of.description: Date the cross-family ordering was established or last re-verified. A vendor capability page changes when the next model ships, so this date bounds the claim.

source.description: Vendor page the capability ordering was read from.

note.description: Which declared pairs are vendor-stated, which come from an operator ruling, and which are inherited without a citation.

inherited_pairs.description: Cross-family pairs whose order is inherited from a previously shipped rank table and carries no citation. Each entry is [higher, lower] by row key.

effort_exempt_sentinels.description: Values that legally appear where a pinned model ID is expected but are not models and never get a row, so no row-derived list can produce them. Every generated effort-exemption list is the union of these and the `effort_exempt` rows, and is asserted to contain each of these.

models.description: The rows, keyed by pinned full model ID. Key order carries no meaning: the document is key-sorted for byte-stability, and every ordering question is answered by `generation` or `cross_family_rank`.

modelId.description: Bare pinned full model ID: family segment then one or more numeric generation segments. Never an alias (`opus`), never a `-YYYYMMDD` snapshot suffix, never a `[1m]` window selector — a caller strips those before lookup.

priceTable.description: Per-million-token rates for one price basis. All five rates are required together: a partial table cannot be costed.

family.description: Family segment of the row key (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`, ...). Deliberately not an enum: a new family is a data change, not a schema change. Two rows are same-family when this value matches exactly.

generation.description: Numeric generation segments of the row key, most significant first: `claude-opus-4-8` is [4, 8] and `claude-opus-5` is [5]. Sole input to within-family ordering, compared element-wise with a prefix ranking below its extension.

release_date.description: Vendor release (snapshot) date, or null when none is published or recorded. Never an ordering input — a null cannot perturb any comparison.

context_window.description: Maximum input tokens the model accepts. This is capacity, not the runtime default: a caller opts into a window above the runtime default with the `[1m]` selector on the pinned ID.

knowledge_cutoff.description: Reliable knowledge cutoff as YYYY-MM, or null when the vendor publishes none.

min_cacheable_prefix.description: Shortest prompt prefix that can be cached, in tokens. A shorter prefix cannot be cached at all, so a caller batching small prompts checks this before paying a cache-write rate.

batch_discount.description: Multiplier applied to every rate when the request runs through the Batches API (0.5 = half price).

price.description: Both price bases for this row. A consumer prefers `contract` over `list` whenever `contract` is non-null; a row with both null has no sourced rate and costing it resolves roster-stale.

list.description: Public list rates, or null when none is sourced for this row.

contract.description: Negotiated rates. Reserved: null on every row until a contract rate exists.

effort_available.description: Effort levels a plan may pin for this model, listed low to max — the allowlist an effort check projects, so a level absent here is rejected for this model unless `effort_exempt` is set. A model that ignores the effort parameter still lists the levels a plan may pin for it, because the roster records what is accepted, not what changes behavior.

effort_exempt.description: True when effort checks skip this model entirely rather than testing `effort_available`. No other field derives it, which is why it is declared per row; values that need the same exemption but have no row are named in `effort_exempt_sentinels`.

lifecycle.description: Vendor lifecycle state. Independent of `selectable`: a model the vendor lists as legacy but has not deprecated stays `active` here, and deprecation is the vendor's act, not a selection policy.

deprecation_date.description: Date the vendor deprecates or deprecated this model. Non-null exactly when `lifecycle` is `deprecated`.

selectable.description: Selection policy, independent of `lifecycle`. `new-work` — a plan may pin it; `legacy-pin-only` — an existing pin stays valid but a plan may not choose it; `retired` — no surface may name it. The plan-schema enum projects from `new-work`; the authoring gate's allowlist projects from everything but `retired`.

cross_family_rank.description: Declared capability rank used ONLY to compare rows of different families, higher being more capable. Null means this row's cross-family order is undeclared, so any cross-family comparison against it is roster-stale — a human judgment is visible as data instead of a heuristic guessing it. Never consulted for a same-family comparison.

notes.description: Row-level vendor caveat a field cannot carry (an introductory rate window, a dated full ID, why a field is null). Non-load-bearing: no projection reads it.
